title: Dragon's Dogma 2's August Update Finally Adds Multiple Save Slots, One For Each Arisen - NewsBreak
text:
By Franz Christian Irorita ,
3 hours ago
Dragon's Dogma 2 is finally fixing one of its most-criticized launch decisions.
Capcom has confirmed that the game's free late-August update will increase the number of save slots from one to three, letting players keep several separate Arisen going at the same time.
To be precise: this gives you room for up to three different Arisen, or playthroughs, rather than multiple saves of a single character.
Each of the three slots is tied to its own Arisen, and a new slot is only created when you begin a fresh adventure with a new one, so you cannot spin up several parallel saves of the same character.
Within each slot, the game keeps three types of save data: an Autosave, an Interim Save, and a Last Inn Rest Save, and loading from your last inn rest will no longer wipe out your autosave or interim save.
Save slots also will not be deleted automatically anymore. In other words, the design still holds to Dragon's Dogma's philosophy that a given Arisen's journey is largely permanent, but you are no longer locked into a single character on your account.
That distinction matters because the single-save-slot setup was one of the loudest complaints at launch.
Out of the gate, Dragon's Dogma 2 shipped without a straightforward way to start a new playthrough short of overwriting your existing progress, which was extra frustrating given the performance issues at launch. Being able to simply keep three Arisen on the go is the kind of quality-of-life basics players have wanted since day one.
What's in Dragon's Dogma 2's Free August Update? The save change is only one part of a meatier free update.
The same late-August patch finally adds a way to cure Dragonsplague, the dangerous condition that could quietly kill your Main Pawn and wipe out an entire town's NPCs, through a new item called the Dragonsbaulk Draught.
It also bumps the number of assignable active weapon skills from four to six, giving each vocation more flexibility, alongside broad performance, UI, and balance improvements.
It follows June's update , which introduced the Eternal Ferrystone for unlimited fast travel and pared back several microtransactions.
Dragon's Dogma 2 is set for a Comeback All of this is groundwork for a larger comeback.
The August update is the second of two big free patches leading into the paid Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen expansion, which we covered when Capcom revealed it as a massive new expansion and a Nintendo Switch 2 release for October 9 .
Between the frozen Norgan region arriving with the expansion and this steady stream of quality-of-life fixes, Capcom is clearly running a soft-relaunch to win back players who bounced off at launch.
The save-slot update lands free for all owners ahead of that October push.
